title: Wang Zhenyi
summary: Wang Zhenyi (1768–1797) was a Qing-dynasty astronomer and mathematician whose home was in present-day Nanjing. She wrote on lunar eclipses, the Pythagorean theorem and trigonometry, and the roundness of the Earth, and her Simple Principles of Calculations was published when she was 24. Most of her work was lost. A crater on Venus was named for her in 1994.

uncertainty.note: Only years are given in the sources, not exact dates.

where.historical_name: Nanjing, Qing China (East China; home where she did her experiments, per the University of Edinburgh)

importance.justification: A woman astronomer and mathematician of eighteenth-century China whose surviving writings explain eclipses and argue for a spherical Earth.
